findings.title: Old returned reservation Drop can erase a new runtime reservation claim

evidence.detail: physical_returned sets returned=true and runtime_owned=false, then Drop unconditionally stores false again for returned reservations.
poll calls reservation.physical_returned while retaining the Arc in the old RuntimeOwner, so its final Drop can be delayed until after a later reservation is acquired.
A new reservation only CASes the shared bool false-to-true; ownership is not bound to an exact reservation identity.
configuration_edit relies on runtime_owned while state.enabled is false; reserve_runtime similarly relies on it.

constructibleSequence: Reserve old, mark started, activate; negative stop and settle state.enabled=false.
Call old.physical_returned but retain an old Arc/RuntimeOwner.
Reserve fresh: runtime_owned becomes true; before fresh activate state.enabled remains false.
Drop final old Arc: old returned=true causes Drop to overwrite runtime_owned=false.

configuration_edit or another reserve_runtime can now pass while fresh still owns its original reservation and may be opening a native listener. The same window exists during fresh stop after enabled=false but before physical return.
findings.impactScope: Normal Running state.enabled=true still separately rejects configuration edits; this finding does not claim that check is bypassed. The ordinary UI currently drops its old owner before preparing its replacement, but public runtime/service ownership must remain correct under legal delayed old-owner Drop.
findings.minimalFix: Release claim exactly once for the original reservation, preferably bind it to a monotonic reservation identity/CAS. In particular, a returned reservation Drop must not clear a newer claim. Add a real service/session regression retaining old returned Arc across fresh reserve and proving both save and another reserve remain Busy after old drop.
findings.notExecuted: This is a source-derived constructible schedule; no repro test was executed in this read-only task.
findings.notifications: Root and production_backend were sent immediate source finding and narrowed enabled-state impact before this report.

confirmedStaticProperties.item: Original native third cleanup fault crosses HTTP generations
confirmedStaticProperties.evidence: A third native.rs Owner cleanup_failed and process OWNER_FAULTED; B run maps ConfiguredTlsError::Cleanup to early_return physical=false and retains reservation.
confirmedStaticProperties.conclusion: The old HTTP thread cannot clear native static fault by exiting; startup Cleanup does not become physical-returned proof.

Running tickets remain until is_finished plus actual result. Net idle requires native_drained and no records. Runtime then additionally requires stopped sessions, physically returned cleanup ticket and both Hub registries/quarantine empty before dropping original Net/Hub owners and marking returned.

Negative domain stop cancels exact Owned/Busy lifetimes. Fresh worker cleanup leases only Owned entries; Busy entries remain counted. MaterialReady/retained cleanup checks exact app binding and token; download close_entry runs on worker holding actual pin. This review does not assert actual IO disposal without runtime evidence.

confirmedStaticProperties.evidence: network.rs:1190-1237,1242-1274; uploads.rs key_for_request and cleanup_request; downloads.rs cleanup_request
confirmedStaticProperties.conclusion: Begin submission marks hub_touched before positive reply. Canceled/suppressed reply does not erase actual Running ticket; cleanup by original request token follows actual completion and can recover the Hub entry even without returned key.

confirmedStaticProperties.item: Stop origin and UI physical wait
confirmedStaticProperties.conclusion: Repeated stop stores minimum original timestamp; five-second fault does not start a new positive owner. Runtime joins only after physical_thread observer reports original HANDLE terminated. New negative cleanup job slices do not renew stored stop_at budget.

Negative epoch and browser session revocation precede new epoch admission. SQL guard checks negative runtime before waiting ledger and again after authorization; old exact sessions are revoked before new activate. Permission state is separate from public desktop buttons.
